P-Zero Research's new TasteVal benchmark measures research taste: how well a model designs experiments and reads their results on eight real AI-development tasks, scored by how much compute it needs compared with human experts (the dashed 1x line). 

Progress was slow from GPT-4 in 2023 through 2025, then the slope steepened: since December 2025, scores have doubled every 3.0 months. Claude Opus 5.5 now sits at 2.30x the expert baseline, ahead of Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, at roughly 1/30 of the experts' cost per attempt.

Research taste is the skill that decides how quickly AI could start improving AI, and this curve is one reason Jack Clark now expects that in 2027 (wrote about that yesterday as well).

If you don't use the models or watch the demos people post on social media, you may not realize there has been an astonishing jump in game development capability lately. We really are not that far away from a one-person game studio anymore.

You can mash up games now and the model will deliver a stable, playable fusion in one day. Some of them are so good that people don't post them openly online because they are afraid of getting sued. That's how quickly things have improved over the last few weeks with Astra and Opus 5.5.

Because of how virulently anti-AI the game industry has become, people are going to get completely blindsided by what's about to arrive. Not only are they unaware of how fast things are improving, they don't seem to understand the endgame. I see people taking about supply gluts, things like that.  This isn't about making games to sell on Steam and compete with the industry. If the player knows the type of game they want, and their model can code that game for them at the AAA level, in the genre they ask for, with the aesthetics and character design they prefer, then the question becomes: why buy a game from a studio at all?

I think Sir Demis sees this future with Genie. For the price of your subscription, you will get any style of game you want, tailored to you. Once that starts happening at scale, most game studios will very rapidly cease to exist. And that's the real endgame. Not competition; destruction. And it's closer than people think.

Grok Imagine can now generate amazing custom music directly for your videos... and it's incredibly easy to use 🎵

Here's how to add music:

1. Generate your video in Grok Imagine
2. Click the music icon at the top
3. Select “+ Add music”
4. Describe the music you want....mood, tempo, instruments, vocals or no vocals, or simply write your own prompt
5. Click Generate
6. Preview your generated music
7. Select the section that fits your video
8. Click Apply

And the best part is that your generated music is automatically saved to your library, so you can reuse it in future videos too

Video generation and custom soundtracks in the same workflow

OpenAI’s next flagship faces safety hurdles. OpenAI reportedly diverted 10% of its compute to safety.

According to The Information, OpenAI is working to make its next flagship safe to release after canceling a less capable model over safety concerns.

The successor reportedly uses loop transformers, which repeatedly process problems internally but can make reasoning harder to monitor. Following the Hugging Face incident, OpenAI redirected roughly 10% of its compute toward alignment and safety.

The model would also undergo US government testing, potentially adding up to 30 days before release. Employees still expect one or two new models by year-end, even if the flagship isn’t ready.
